select_when: Execution requires persistence across a long sequence of small decisions that would otherwise unravel under distraction or drift.
The commitment is tied to a reversible experiment, disciplined cadence, or identity-based habit that benefits from staying power.
The main risk is under-follow-through rather than over-escalation, and the team has explicit stop rules to revisit the commitment.
A person or group is defending a prior commitment, identity, or promise more strongly than the evidence now justifies.
Escalation, rigidity, or self-justification is blocking reversal even though the original assumptions have weakened.
The real issue is not lack of information but the social or psychological cost of admitting the earlier choice may have been wrong.
The team needs to inspect how small public commitments are shaping larger downstream behavior.
avoid_when: Prior public commitment, sunk cost, or ego investment is becoming more important than updating on new evidence.
The case demands flexibility and fast updating, but the commitment structure would make reversal socially or politically expensive.
The model is being used to mock consistency itself instead of distinguishing disciplined persistence from self-deceptive lock-in.

curation_notes.summary: Merged from commitment-bias (persistence vs escalation lens) and commitment-and-consistency-bias (self-justification and rigidity lens). The merged model covers both constructive persistence and pathological lock-in.
donor_drops: Dropped donor long-tail case examples that repeated the same escalation pattern without adding structural distinction.
Dropped donor higher-order relation overlays to keep the batch-2 contract frozen.
Did not widen into generic commitment or culture rhetoric because the raw source is strongest on rationalization, group loyalty, and reversal difficulty.
open_questions: The typed fields compress a source distinction between healthy persistence and unhealthy escalation into a reviewed operational interface.
The source mixes productive consistency with pathological rigidity, so the avoid conditions work hard to keep the curated use narrow.

select_when.note: The first three triggers come from the persistence/escalation lens; the last four from the self-justification/rigidity lens. Both are explicit in the merged raw source.

avoid_when.note: Combined anti-activation rules from both source models. The first two are escalation-risk rules; the third prevents mocking consistency itself.

input_type.note: The source presents a persistence-versus-update decision boundary, but the exact input label is reviewed normalization.

output_type.note: The raw file implies a stop-rule-aware commitment check rather than a generic bias label; the output label operationalizes that function.

reasoning_types.note: Diagnostic and causal from the persistence lens; metacognitive added from the self-justification lens which requires inspecting one's own commitment stories.
